# tweetly

> Multi-tenant X (Twitter) automation platform for AI agents. Connect one or more X accounts, then drive them programmatically over MCP or REST: post, reply, like, retweet, quote, follow, bookmark, search, and monitor — all backed by a real browser session, not the X API.

tweetly speaks two languages:
- **MCP** — drop the server into Claude / Cursor / any MCP client and your agent can act on X with natural-language tool calls.
- **REST** — bearer-authenticated HTTP API (`tk_*` keys) for any agent or backend that prefers raw HTTP.

The same Zod schemas back both surfaces, so a tool name in MCP maps 1:1 to a route in REST.

## Self-hosting

This is an open-source project. The official source and setup instructions are at <https://github.com/beydemirfurkan/tweetly>.

When deploying on your own infrastructure, this `llms.txt` is served from the panel domain. Override it (or replace the URLs below) with your own deployment endpoints — the defaults are placeholders.

## API

- API Reference (Scalar): served at `<your-backend>/docs` once deployed.
- OpenAPI spec: `<your-backend>/api/openapi.json` — machine-readable JSON; consume with codegen, Postman, Insomnia, or your own tooling.
- Auth: bearer tokens issued from `POST /auth/api-keys`. Format: `Authorization: Bearer tk_...`.
- OAuth resource metadata: `<your-backend>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

## MCP

The MCP server is mounted at `<your-backend>/mcp`. It exposes ~43 tools backed by the same Zod schemas as the REST API.

### Write tools (queue-backed actions)
- `post_tweet`, `reply_to_tweet`, `quote_tweet`, `post_thread`
- `like_tweet` / `unlike_tweet`, `retweet_tweet` / `unretweet_tweet`, `bookmark_tweet`
- `follow_account` / `unfollow_account`
- `delete_tweet`, `send_dm`
- `update_profile`, `update_avatar`, `update_banner`

### Read tools (synchronous lookups)

List-style reads return `{ items, nextCursor }`. Pass `nextCursor` back as the `cursor` argument to fetch subsequent pages; cursors are opaque (don't parse them). Single-resource reads return their plain shape.

- `search_tweets`, `search_users`, `get_user`, `get_tweet`
- `get_user_tweets`, `get_user_followers`, `get_user_following`
- `get_tweet_retweeters`, `get_tweet_quotes`, `get_tweet_replies`
- `get_user_mentions`, `get_x_trending`, `get_user_likes`, `get_my_bookmarks`
- `get_list_members`, `get_list_subscribers`, `get_list`, `get_user_lists`
- `get_mutual_followers`, `get_thread`

### Monitors
- `create_monitor`, `list_monitors`, `get_monitor`, `pause_monitor`, `delete_monitor`

### Bulk extractions (async, file output)

Queue large jobs that run a cursor-paginated read endpoint to completion (up to 100K rows). Output is JSONL on the server; download via REST.

- `create_extraction`, `get_extraction`, `list_extractions`, `cancel_extraction`

Supported `type` values: `user_followers`, `user_following`, `user_tweets`, `user_likes`, `user_mentions`, `tweet_retweeters`, `search_tweets`, `list_members`. Download endpoint is REST-only: `GET /api/v1/extractions/{id}/download`.

### Accounts, jobs, settings
- `get_accounts`, `get_account_health`
- `connect_x_account`, `reauth_x_account`, `get_x_login_job`
- `list_actions`, `cancel_action`, `replay_action`
- `get_settings`, `update_settings`
